heroHeadline: Taiwan Pushes Back After Trump Stays Silent on $14B Arms Package Following Xi Summit; PLA Sorties Fell to 2 as Xi Departed Washington
heroSubtitle: Taiwan Deputy Foreign Minister Francois Wu told reporters in Taipei on September 26, 2026 that maintaining US arms sales and Taiwan's semiconductor role 'are important US interests,' pushing back after President Trump's three-day Washington summit with Xi Jinping ended September 25 with no public decision on the paused $14 billion arms package and no comment from Trump on Taiwan since. Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs had separately rejected Xi's Taiwan remarks to Trump on September 25 as a 'distortion of facts.' Taiwan's MND recorded just 2 PLA aircraft sorties (1 crossing the median line) in the 24 hours to September 25 — down sharply from 10 sorties on both September 23 and 24 — as Xi concluded his visit and departed; the summit's clearest concrete outcome was a two-month extension of the US-China trade truce.
